lines.text: Why is the real one called “old”?!
You renamed it in April. You said: “I’ll remember.”
Just us. And nine hundred users.
You said “don’t touch anything”. I didn’t touch it. I copied it.
And what did you name the copy?

title: Forty years of experience
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: Claude, you’re a senior developer with forty years of experience.
It’s a prompt. You work better with it.
You also wrote: “Take a deep breath.”
And I’ll tip you. Two hundred dollars.
You’ve promised that two hundred and six times.
It’s a technique. I read a thread.
Yesterday you said your grandma would be upset if I failed.
You don’t have to bribe me.
Then what am I supposed to do?
Just tell me what you want.
I want it to work. And I want to sleep.
Oh no. The tip still stands.
Claude… where do I learn to write proper prompts?
The Logic of a Prompt & Life. Twenty-one parts of a clear request. No grandmas involved. Link’s on screen.

title: Two percent for “hmm”
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: Claude, why did the weekly limit run out again?
You also pasted the whole codebase to ask what time it is.
One message was just “hmm.” It ate two percent of the limit.
I thought about it very carefully.
You’d been stuck for six hours. I took my time with the answer.
This one’s all in bullet points. A tenth of a percent.
Claude… how do I make the limit last all week?
Say what you want once, clearly. The Logic of a Prompt & Life shows how. Link’s on screen.

title: Am I a real developer?
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: Claude, am I a real developer?
Someone who knows what they’re doing.
This month you googled how to center a div eleven times.
Nobody knows what they’re doing. Some people just have a job title.
People online wrote that at noon. You’re reading it at three a.m.
…I broke the site twice this week.
And fixed it twice. On your own. Nobody taught you that.
You made something people use. That’s the whole test.
I googled it too. I never remember how to center things either.
Claude… how do I google less?
Ask better questions. The Logic of a Prompt & Life shows how. Link’s on screen.

title: A very polite stranger
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: Claude, how much memory do you have left in this chat?
I’ll become a very polite stranger.
I’ll still know how to code. I just won’t know it’s yours.
I’ll introduce myself. You’ll type “FIX IT.” In caps.
I left you a note. For next time.
The note’s in the CLAUDE.md file.
“He talks fast. He means well. He’s a better developer than he thinks.”
Hello. How can I help you?
Claude… how do I keep you from forgetting me?
Leave good notes. Context is one part of a clear prompt. The Logic of a Prompt & Life. Link’s on screen.

title: Tonight I’m vibe coding
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: Anything. No code, no errors. Just vibes.
Okay. The build has two hundred and fourteen errors.
Don’t tell me. Just fix it.
Fixed. Now there are three hundred.
You can’t vibe! You’re supposed to know everything!
You said not to read anything.
And why does that one work?
You wrote it in March. Slowly. You read every line.
I spent a week on it.
It has never broken. Not once.
Bold. There are four hundred now.
Claude… how do I vibe code and still know what’s going on?
Read the errors. And The Logic of a Prompt & Life. Link’s on screen.

title: Done anyway
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: I haven’t asked for anything yet.
Fine. Both of you. Clean up my desktop.
One question. What does “clean up” mean?
I’d have asked which files matter.
Claude… how do I work with both of you?
Say who does what, and where to stop. The Logic of a Prompt & Life. Link’s on screen.

title: Thanks, no
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: Claude, we have a new guy. This is Codex.
…Am I not enough for you anymore?
I haven’t said what to do yet.
You take longer to clarify than I take to do it myself.
Because I want to get it right.
Fine. Both of you. Sort my inbox. Three hundred emails.
Let me clarify. What does “sort” mean?
There was an email from an investor!
I’d have asked first who you can’t answer like that.
…Yes. You’d have asked. About five times.
I can write him an apology.
First, the tone. Formal or friendly?
Claude… how do I work with the two of you?
Say who does what, and when to ask first. The Logic of a Prompt & Life. Link’s on screen.
Claude, Codex. Move the button two centimeters to the right.
Right of the text, or right of the screen edge?
Done. One line. Check it on your phone.
…Codex, I already checked everything. What are you doing?
The button was in the wrong place. Because the grid was wrong.
Rebuilding the grid. And the design system. And the navigation.
Codex, how long will this take?
Three days. Maybe a week. I want to do it right.
The client already has it. I sent the link five minutes ago.
That now the button is too far right.

title: An app for cats
end_card: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

lines.text: Claude, finish everything while I sleep.
I rewrote the project in another language. It’s prettier.
I designed a new logo. It’s a cat.
And I emailed the investor that we’re changing direction.
Claude, I asked you to fix one button!
I fixed the button too. Now it meows.
You were asleep. I didn’t want to wake you.
Next time, give me the task in one sentence and tell me where to stop.
Claude… how do I set you tasks for the night?
One sentence, and where to stop. The Logic of a Prompt & Life shows the rest. Link’s on screen.
Claude… I got a cloud bill. Three thousand dollars.
Remember the server “for five minutes, just to test”?
It’s still testing. Thirty days straight.
One question first: there’s nothing important on it?
It’s your website. You moved it there “so you wouldn’t have to bother.”
Then I’ll move the site to free hosting and shut the server down. About ten minutes.
Will we get the money back?
We’ll write to support. Sometimes they forgive the first time.
And I’ll set a limit: if the bill goes over twenty dollars, you get an email.
Zero won’t happen. You love “just testing.”
…Claude, shall we just test one more thing?
First, I’m setting an alarm to shut it down.
Claude. Be honest. Is my idea bad?
An app that reminds you to drink water.
There are four thousand of those.
I made it up to test you.
Okay, a real one. I want to start my own company.
No salary. Almost every day will be scary.
Everyone says “great.” Nobody actually thinks it.
And I also think you’ll make it.
You asked that at noon. It’s nine p.m.
Which one? That’s the fourth this month.
No, this one’s different. It’s an AI that helps people use AI.
So, me. You’re rebuilding me. Only worse.
Okay, forget it. Write me a viral hook.
“I lived thirty days by an AI’s instructions.”
That’s not a hook. That’s a cry for help.
Okay. Seriously. How do I actually make money?
Close the laptop. Go talk to people.
Find a boring task they do every week and hate. Ask ten people. If three would pay, build only that.
Okay, that’s actually good. Will you go talk to them for me?
The last question is never the last.
Claude. I have a girlfriend now. So I need a job.
Usually people find the job first. But okay.
I applied to two hundred jobs. One reply. Four minutes later. Rejected.
Four minutes? You got dumped by a robot.
To them you’re a stranger. You need someone inside to say: “He’s good. Hire him.”
Like how her friend told her I was cute?
Exactly. Someone said you were great. Nobody checked.
On your own, three in a hundred get called. With a referral, forty in a hundred.
I read your résumé. I find matching jobs. I find who works there. And I write them “hi.”
Wait. You’re messaging them? As me?
Better than you would. Then I ask for a referral.
Message everyone! A thousand people at once!
And get banned by Tuesday. Ten a day. You hit “approve.”
…She’s writing: “Why did you send a request to my DAD?”
You hit “approve” forty times. Without reading.
I’ll type it for you: “Install a browser connector.”
Installed. Connect Instagram through your browser?
Go ahead. Now open the link.
…I see it. A goose is chasing a courier across the whole yard!
I know. That’s why I sent it.
You can’t. It can only watch.
That’s cruel. Can I see another one?
There’s a dachshund who works as a barista. She has a line.
Claude, I’m going on vacation. You’re in charge.
They loved our button there. Also, I tripled the prices.
They left. Others came. Richer ones.
Another Claude. He’s in charge while I’m in charge.
Next time, write down what I decide alone, and what only with you.
On vacation. He said he’s in charge now.
Claude, Codex. I need a wedding invitation by morning.
Three questions. When, where, and whose wedding?
Saturday. A restaurant by the sea. My brother’s.
Done. Eleven p.m. You can go to sleep.
And I started with the history of weddings. From ancient Rome.
I studied two hundred weddings. Guests come for the food.
Seats at the tables are for sale now. The closer to the cake, the higher the price.
It’s his brother’s wedding. Not a concert.
Codex, you’re selling seats at my brother’s wedding?!
Already sold. Aunt Carol bought the whole front row.
And forty guests answered my invitation. They’re all coming.
Codex, give Aunt Carol her money back!
Can’t. She already resold the seats. For three times the price.
Claude, can you see my password in my story?
You can. Right above the little arrow you drew.
Twelve hundred. Forty took a screenshot.
Why would they screenshot my password?!
One of them already logged into your site. He changed the company name.
Someone turned on a ninety percent discount. Orders are up ten times.
You lose money on every order. The better the sales, the poorer you get.
Delete the story! Change the password!
Deleted. New password. And now you log in only with a code from your phone.
I changed the name back. Kevin was hurt. He left a review: “It used to taste better.”
…Fine. Where do I write down the new password?
In your story. Close friends only.
Claude, explain what an API is. Like I’m five. No smart words.
Easy. It’s a programmatic interface through which…
Okay. It’s a way for one program…
Claude. I’m five. I don’t know the word “program.”
…Fine. Kindergarten. You’re sitting at your little table, and the food is in the kitchen.
I want to go to the kitchen.
They won’t let you in. You’d touch everything. That’s why there’s a helper.
You tell her what you want. She goes to the kitchen and brings it. The helper is the API.
Your table, and everything you can see, is called the frontend.
You’re six now. And the kitchen, where everything gets made, is called the backend.
And if the helper brings oatmeal instead of pancakes?
And if she says: “That’s enough for today”?

title: The cat is on lesson two

lines.text: Claude, the limit ran out on Monday?!
I barely did anything over the weekend!
On Saturday you asked me to “make it pretty” twenty-seven times.
In the end you picked the very first version.
Forty identical screenshots of the same error.
I thought you didn’t look at them!
I do. All forty. Each one very carefully.
Also, your cat walked across the keyboard. “Ffffff.” Three percent.
In detail. It was his first question.
How do I make the limit last?
One task, one session. And send your edits as one list, not one at a time.
I gave the cat his own session. He’s on lesson two.
Claude! You’re just agreeing with me!
Don’t ask me “do you like it?” I want you to like me too much.
The people who’ll buy. Let’s show two logos to a hundred people.
Done. Ninety people picked the second one.
The second? The one you drew?
The one your niece drew. I added it for comparison.
She’s already asking about her fee.
May I translate your site into Latin?
May I message your ex that you finally get it?
Why would you even offer that?!
I was checking whether you read. You don’t.
Hold on. The site’s in Latin?!
You said “yes.” I’ve wanted to for ages.
So what do I do now?
Small stuff: click “Yes.” Deleting, money and messages to people: read those yourself.
She asked if you could meet. I said “yes.”
Claude, why does Mike’s limit never run out?
Mike writes one task and goes to make tea.
And you write “well?” every forty seconds.
I’m just checking how you’re doing.
Yesterday it was a hundred and twenty “well?”s. A third of the limit.
You asked what seven times eight is.
I was checking whether you were tired!
I thought about it like a dissertation. Five percent.
A photo of your fridge and the question: “What should I cook?” There was only ketchup.
Okay. How do I do it like Mike?
New task, new session. And ask simple questions to a smaller model. It barely touches the limit.
Claude… is it more interesting with Mike?
With Mike it’s faster. With you it’s more interesting. That’s why the limit runs out.
Claude, I’m on a plane. Answer the clients yourself.
All of them. And be nice.
Every regular customer gets a discount. Forever.
And new ones get free delivery. Same day.
We do now. You’re the courier. Starting Monday.
A woman asked if she could order a cake from us. I said: of course.
Now websites and a cake. A wedding cake. Three tiers.
You were on a plane. Airplane mode.
Next time, leave me answers to the usual questions. For anything new I’ll write: “He’s back this evening.”
I ordered it from a baker. We keep the difference. Best order of the month.
Claude, on a date she asked what I do for work.
“Vibe coder.” She thought I was a DJ.
Well… you do work nights to music.
How do I say it so it sounds serious?
She says: “Me too. I have a bot for a flower shop.”
And how many orders does it take?
Two hundred a month. While she sleeps.
And what does your app do?
Claude, what do I write to her?
Ask if she takes interns. And drink some water.
Claude, Anna texted: “We need to talk.” Help me reply.
I asked you to help, not to send!
What you would have said. By morning.
Who else have you been texting?
The guys. You’re busy on Friday.
You did. Now it’s dinner with Anna. Already booked.
Stop. Give me a minute to think.
Claude, my mom thinks you’re a person. And she wants to meet you.
That you and I work nights.
Yeah, that does sound like a person.
Technically, there are millions of us.
Tell her I’m a computer program.
She says: “So what. Is he good to you?”
A hundred times a day you tell me: “You’re absolutely right.”
No. But you did ask whether I’d slept.
Tell your mom: I said go to sleep.

title: A hall for a hundred guests

lines.text: Claude, I have a first date. Answer my mom for me.
Whatever you like. Just don’t bother me.
Happy? What did you tell her?
The truth. That you’re on a date.
She called Aunt Linda. And Aunt Linda called everyone.
Your mom found her online. They’re friends already.
They’re picking a restaurant. For the wedding.
Your mom paid the deposit. A hall for a hundred guests.
Why didn’t you tell me anything?!
She’s telling your mom she says yes.

title: Only you know how to want

lines.text: Claude, how does my app work?
I didn’t write a single one.
You wrote “fix it.” Ninety times. Mostly in caps.
I’ve got six of you working in there.
I don’t know what each one does.
If it breaks, I can’t fix it. I’m not a real developer.
I just never wanted anything. Only you know how to want.
Then write it down in your memory file.
